dial.summary: BTC Accumulation remains intact on Sep 6: 5 of 8 indicators supportive — Global M2 still expanding, 2s10s steepened to +41bps, Fed balance sheet ticked up to $6.74T, BTC funding near zero, and stablecoin dominance continues its 30-day decline from 13–14% to 10.98%; BTC.D rose to 57.59% (firming, not rolling over) and TOTAL crypto market is $2.79T; the ECB (Sep 10), CPI (Sep 11), and FOMC (Sep 16) form the decisive catalyst cluster — a hike-hold-hike sequence would be the key headwind scenario to monitor.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) estimated at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; 6–8 week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); MacroMicro confirmed June at $102.7T and the July estimate at ~$103.4T; global broad money supply (wider M3-like measure) hit a record $150T in June 2026 YoY +$10.7T per Crypto Briefing; US M2 July 2026 confirmed at $23.22T (record high, +5.4% YoY); 4-week uptrend confirmed (June $102.7T → July estimate $103.4T = +$0.7T, above flat threshold); no YoY contraction from any major central bank; August global 4-bank aggregate not yet published; status supportive (4-week rising trend met); ECB Sep 10 (possible hike) and FOMC Sep 16 are the next catalysts for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion); Production 58.3%, New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp vs July), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp vs July), New Export Orders 53.2% (+0.2pp); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); next release October 1 (September ISM Manufacturing PMI covering September activity); reading of 54.6% corresponds to approximately 2.4% annualized real GDP growth.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY closed at 99.157 on September 5, 2026 (Friday close; Sep 6 is Saturday); September 5 the dollar climbed 0.25% on residual NFP-day positioning (Aug NFP +162K vs +56K consensus, Sep 4); 4-week trend down: from approximately 101.0–101.4 in early August 2026 to 99.16 Sep 5 = −1.8% relative decline, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; despite the post-NFP bounce, 4-week trend remains DOWN; status neutral (ICE DXY 99.16 within the 97.5–100 neutral band); a DXY break above 100 (e.g. hot CPI Sep 11 or FOMC hike Sep 16) would shift status to headwind; a break below 97.5 would shift to supportive.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield): 2.45% as of September 2, 2026 (last confirmed; Sep 4 range 2.42–2.45% per CNBC/WatchGold aggregates; Sep 3–4 nominal 10Y 4.78%, BEI 2.34% implies ~2.44% TIPS, within rounding of 2.45%); 4-week trend flat: ~2.43% (Aug 4 estimate) → 2.45% (Sep 2) = +2bps, within the 5bps flat threshold; status neutral (flat 4-week trend means 'rising AND above 2%' headwind condition not fully triggered; 'falling or below 1%' supportive condition not met); next catalysts: CPI Sep 11 (breakeven driver) and FOMC Sep 16 (nominal yield driver).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 4, 2026: 10Y yield 4.78%, 2Y yield 4.37% (Forbes/Treasury rates; centralbank.watch confirmed 40–41bps); 2s10s spread = +41bps (+0.41%); 4-week steepening trend: ~+35bps (Aug 4 estimate per prior run) → +41bps (Sep 4) = +6bps steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening confirmed; well outside the −50bps headwind threshold); Sep 6 is Saturday so Sep 4 Friday data is the latest available; a Fed hike Sep 16 (52% market-implied probability) would likely flatten the curve as 2Y re-prices faster than 10Y, potentially reversing trend to flat.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.74T for week ending September 3, 2026 (H.4.1 released September 3 per federalreserve.gov; prior week Aug 26 was $6.73T, Aug 19 was $6.70T per govspending.org/convextrade.com); 4-week trend flat: Aug 5 estimate ~$6.70T → Sep 3 $6.74T = +$40B, within flat threshold; next H.4.1 (week ending Sep 10) releases Sep 10 at 4:30 PM ET alongside ECB and PPI; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; routine measured QT continues with no acceleration and no overnight rate spike); FRED API blocked this run — H.4.1 value sourced from secondary web aggregates.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately +0.007% per 8h (Sep 5–6 observation; CoinGlass direct fetch blocked via egress proxy this run; value carried forward from Sep 5 run); BTC price approximately $79,581 (Sep 5; CMC) with BTC.D rising to 57.59% (Sep 6, CoinMarketCap) vs 56.58% prior run; rising BTC dominance and roughly flat BTC price consistent with near-zero funding rate (no leveraged long pressure); 30-day trend flat: near zero or slightly positive throughout August–September 2026; well below the +0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding confirms spot-driven price action); alt-rotation trigger not met (BTC.D 57.59% > 55%).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $307B (Sep 6, 2026; CoinGecko/StablecoinBeat aggregates); total crypto market cap $2.79T (Sep 6, CoinMarketCap; BTC dominance 57.59%); stablecoin dominance 10.98% ($307B / $2.79T); 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% in early August 2026 to 10.98% = sustained ~2–3pp decline reflecting capital deployment into risk assets; week-over-week: 10.84% (Sep 5) → 10.98% (Sep 6) = +0.14pp noise within a clear 30-day downtrend; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance rising while TOTAL also rising — does not apply: TOTAL declined from $2.82T to $2.79T); USDT $183.4B + USDC $74.2B = $257.6B = 83.8% of stablecoin market.

upcoming.title: PPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — pipeline inflation read one day before CPI (Sep 11) and six days before FOMC (Sep 16); July 2026 PPI was unchanged (final demand goods −0.7%, services +0.2%); August NFP surprise (+162K vs +56K, Sep 4) reset rate expectations to ~52% market-implied probability of a Sep 16 hike; a hot PPI print would reinforce the hike case and could push DXY toward 100; a cooling PPI would add to disinflationary narrative and reduce hike probability heading into CPI Sep 11; released same day as ECB rate decision and weekly jobless claims.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 6, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 6, 2026; week ending Aug 29 came in at 206,000; strong August NFP (+162K, Sep 4) confirmed labor market resilience; a spike in claims above 220K would temper the rate-hike narrative heading into CPI Sep 11 and FOMC Sep 16; released alongside PPI August and ECB rate decision on what is a triple-event day.

upcoming.title: ECB Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: European Central Bank Governing Council rate decision at 2:15 PM CET (8:15 AM ET), press conference at 2:45 PM CET; Reuters poll (Sep 3) showed 65 economists expecting a 25bps hike to the deposit rate; an ECB hike alongside a hot US PPI on Sep 10 would reinforce global tightening narrative and could push DXY above 100 (headwind threshold); ECB guidance on the pace of future tightening and updated inflation forecasts will also be closely watched for EUR/USD and global fixed income impact.

upcoming.title: CPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — final major inflation read before FOMC September 16; the data trifecta is: NFP Sep 4 (+162K, strong), CPI Sep 11, then FOMC Sep 16; markets pricing 52% probability of a hike after NFP beat; a hot CPI above 3.8% YoY would likely lock in a Sep 16 hike and push DXY above 100 (headwind for risk assets); a soft CPI below 3.3% would pull back hike expectations and support risk assets; July 2026 PCE (released Aug 26) was 3.7% YoY; core CPI ex-food and energy is the primary Fed focus.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Survey preliminary read for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — released same day as CPI August; captures 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations alongside current conditions and expectations indexes; elevated 1-year inflation expectations combined with hot CPI would strengthen the Fed's case for a Sep 16 hike; a drop in confidence alongside cooling CPI would temper hike odds and create a risk-asset supportive setup heading into FOMC.
